paragraphs: The XJ8 was a key part of Jaguar's XJ range through the late 1990s and 2000s, offering V8 power in a more accessible package than the supercharged XJR. It used the naturally aspirated AJ-V8 engine across two generations — the X308 (1997–2003) and the X350 (2002–2009) — with capacities ranging from 3.2 litres to 4.0 litres depending on the market and specification. The AJ-V8 was Jaguar's first all-new V8 design, and while it's a robust engine overall, timing chain components and valve seals are common service items at higher mileage. The XJ8 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace AJ-V8 (naturally aspirated) engines for every XJ8 on the road.

cards.body: A naturally aspirated V8 fitted to the XJ8 from 1997 to 2009 across two generations. The X308 generation used the 3.2-litre and 4.0-litre versions of the AJ-V8, while the later X350 generation continued with the 4.0-litre AJ-V8 before being replaced by the 4.2-litre unit in some markets. We replace timing chains, tensioners, valve seals and gaskets as standard on every AJ-V8 rebuild.
